prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro: high-frequency urban railway (peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; underground and surface). Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC) is primary means of supervising separation, movement authority (MA), service regulation. Control room does strategic regulation; safety-related train/wayside functions do tactical protection.
Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors service, authorizes changes, incident response, directs recovery); Revenue Train Operator (readiness, cab procedures, passenger actions); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server for equipment health, alarm correlation, restoration without bypassing operational authority); Cyber Security Officer (access controls, key management via Cryptographic Key Management Appliance, security event response).
Elements:
- Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: positions, regulation, alarms, command interfaces; sends Crew Login Token Bundle in start-of-duty process.
- North/South District Zone Controllers: compute MA from train location reports, occupancy, field equipment state; send MA to Atlas.
- East/West Junction Interlockings: vital points/signals control; indications go to Atlas as wayside state inputs via safety channels.
- Atlas Onboard Controller (per train), alias Kestrel (drawings): after operator authentication, assumes active control when energized and train integrity valid; supervises ATP, MA processing (checks sequence, applicability, consistency before applying), speed enforcement, door enable, train interface commands. State machine: initialization, protected manual, automatic train operation, fallback, cutout. Compares two odometry channels continuously; degrades mode if divergence exceeds threshold.
- Dual Channel Odometer: independent speed/distance from axle rotation, inertial sensing, calibration; to Atlas.
- Train Radio Modem to Wayside Radio Access Network.
- Safety Data Communication Network: deterministic, segregated, monitored.
- Service Timetable Server: planned data to regulation.
- Passenger Information Gateway: service messages to customer info systems.
- Voice Dispatch Console: fallback voice path.
- Platform Screen Door Controller: exchanges platform interface indications with train control at fitted stations.
Modes: Normal: automatic headway regulation, separation, exceptions to Controller. Degraded: defined safe state, reduced automation, extra human confirmation, conservative moves per rulebook. Loss of location confidence, comms loss, or vital disagreement shall restrict movement until resolved or approved degraded procedure invoked.

Document units:
S033: When odometry confidence is reduced, the onboard functions increase position uncertainty and request operating actions that preserve separation from other trains.
S034: The trainborne interface to propulsion and braking equipment converts safety commands into vehicle-compatible requests while preserving electrical isolation from non-vital circuits.
S035: Brake assurance functions verify service and emergency brake availability by monitoring brake feedback, pneumatic pressure indications, and commanded deceleration response.
S036: During each enforcement cycle, Atlas Onboard Controller recalculates the braking demand needed to keep the train within the authorized movement limits.
S037: Atlas Onboard Controller produces the Brake Curve Checksum Log after validating the active enforcement data set.
S038: Train Radio Modem provides the onboard data radio function and maintains CBTC sessions over Wayside Radio Access Network coverage areas.
S039: The radio subsystem reports link quality, registration state, and session continuity information to Atlas Onboard Controller for use in mode management.
S040: Safety Data Communication Network provides the protected communications transport used by train control messages that require integrity, authentication, and bounded latency.
S041: Safety Data Communication Network sends the Clock Drift Sample Report at defined synchronization intervals.
S042: Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the security material used by onboard communications without changing the safety logic executed on the train.
S043: The operator interface presents movement authority limits, permitted speed, train location confidence, radio condition, and required operator actions to Revenue Train Operator.
S044: Acknowledgements entered by Revenue Train Operator are passed to Atlas Onboard Controller through a monitored input path that rejects stale or inconsistent commands.
S045: Voice Dispatch Console remains operationally separate from the vital CBTC data path, but it provides a means for voice coordination during degraded service.
S046: Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges door enable and closed-and-locked indications with the train interface when the train is correctly berthed at a platform.
S047: Passenger Information Gateway receives non-vital train position and service state data through an interface that prevents passenger systems from influencing safety decisions.
S048: Service Timetable Server provides schedule context to Metro Operations Control System and related non-vital functions, while onboard enforcement remains based on safety authority and train state.
S049: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server is referred to in some maintenance work instructions as Quarry, but this document uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server as the canonical name.
S050: Maintenance Diagnostic Server collects non-vital health indications from trainborne equipment so that Signal Maintenance Engineer can review faults without connecting directly to vital processing functions.
